name: Semapa Next
prepared_for: Michal Mashall and the Semapa Next platform team
position: Semapa Next is the venture arm of the Semapa group. It backs Series A companies across Europe that aim to become global category leaders, with a portfolio spread over Portugal, the UK, Germany and the Netherlands. Its platform team supports founders on three pillars: access to experts and the group's network, leadership (coaching, senior hires, product, engineering and sales organisation) and finance.
lede: I'm a Lisbon-based Product & RevOps manager. Your Series A companies are at the point where product and revenue operations have to scale, and three of them, Sonant, LOQR and JUPUS, sit right on top of what I've built.
summary: Series A is the stage where a product that works has to become a product and revenue engine that scales: clearer discovery, a roadmap tied to metrics, and a sales and CS stack that doesn't break. That is the exact job I've done for nine years, from AI-powered KYC at 14M-user scale to customer operations at a New York ad-tech platform. Sonant, LOQR and JUPUS sit right on top of my experience, and your Leadership pillar is where I can plug in: as a fractional product lead, a RevOps project, or a full-time hire.

reasons.title: Your stage is my sweet spot
reasons.body: You invest at Series A, when PM and RevOps practices need to professionalise fast. I've built both: specs, roadmaps and squads on one side, CRM, health scores and onboarding automation on the other.

reasons.title: AI in production, not in decks
reasons.body: I've shipped an LLM feature with its evaluation set and production guardrails, and ML and reinforcement-learning features judged on F1. That maps to Sonant, JUPUS, Defined.ai and overstory.

reasons.title: An extension of your Leadership pillar
reasons.body: Your platform already helps founders with senior hires and product, engineering and sales organisation. I'm a Lisbon-based operator you can put in front of a founder this month, in French, English or Portuguese.

vc_notes.thesis: Sector-agnostic, but the portfolio leans climate and industrial, where my overlap is thinner.
vc_notes.stage: Series A: the stage where a senior PM or RevOps lead changes the trajectory.
vc_notes.platform: Dedicated Head of Platform and a Leadership pillar that includes senior talent.

companies.name: Sonant
companies.desc: AI receptionist that handles scheduling, call routing and quote intake for insurance agencies.
companies.why: Voice-AI agents sold to SMB agencies, seed-funded in 2025: I've shipped LLM features with evals and guardrails, and set up the onboarding and CS tooling a young SaaS needs.

companies.name: LOQR
companies.desc: Customer-facing platform that helps banks digitise onboarding and offer compliant services.
companies.why: Bank onboarding and compliance is the product I scaled at Pi Network: ID capture, liveness, fraud and edge cases from about 1M to 14M+ verified users.

companies.name: JUPUS
companies.desc: AI secretariat that automates law-firm work, from the first client call to the finished document.
companies.why: Fresh €13M Series A (June 2026) and an LLM product sold to SMB law firms: the right moment to structure discovery, evals and the sales and CS stack.

companies.name: Defined.ai
companies.desc: Training data and infrastructure for AI development.
companies.why: I know the buyer side of training data: I've trained and evaluated ML models and run human-review loops in KYC, where label quality decides the product.

companies.name: Flecto
companies.desc: Platform that runs rental operations and multiple sales channels for the access economy.
companies.why: Vertical SaaS with payments built in for SMBs: onboarding automation and CS tooling are what I set up at Hop-Place and Vibe.co.

companies.name: Spoke
companies.desc: Delivery software that makes last-mile logistics faster and simpler.
companies.why: Last-mile routing is location tech: I was PM on HEROW's geofencing SDK and platform for iOS and Android.

companies.name: Meisterwerk
companies.desc: Mobile and desktop app that helps craft businesses manage projects, quotes, invoicing and staff.
companies.why: Mobile and web SaaS for SMBs with invoicing: activation, onboarding and the RevOps stack behind a high-volume SMB motion.

companies.name: overstory
companies.desc: Machine learning on satellite imagery to assess forests and vegetation risk for utilities.
companies.why: A geospatial data product like HEROW's, with ML evaluation I've done hands-on. Less overlap on the long utilities sales cycle.

companies.name: Sybilion
companies.desc: Predictive forecasting for textile and fashion, built on anonymised market data.
companies.why: Data-product discovery and turning a forecasting service into a productised SaaS.

companies.name: Fero
companies.desc: Working-capital and stock-management software for the wine and spirits industry.
companies.why: Embedded finance for one vertical: fintech flows plus an SMB sales motion, both in my background.

companies.name: Airly
companies.desc: Sensor network and SaaS that deliver hyper-local air-pollution data.
companies.why: I'd help on the SaaS and data layer and on B2B customer success, less on the hardware.

companies.name: Kencko
companies.desc: Organic fruit and vegetable products, flash-frozen and slow-dried from whole plant foods.
companies.why: Consumer subscription: retention and web-to-app funnel work fits, the food supply chain doesn't.

companies.name: Gigaton
companies.desc: AI-driven decarbonisation of cement pyroprocesses that cuts energy waste and emissions.
companies.why: Strong AI angle, but heavy industry is far from my track record.

companies.name: Constellr
companies.desc: Satellite imaging beyond the visible spectrum to monitor vegetation, soil, water, carbon and industrial activity.
companies.why: Overlap on the data product only; satellite hardware sits outside my experience.

companies.name: GROPYUS
companies.desc: Technology-driven builder of sustainable, affordable homes, from design to asset management.
companies.why: Limited overlap with my software-product background.

companies.name: Oceano Fresco
companies.desc: Sustainable seafood company farming bivalves with aquaculture techniques.
companies.why: No meaningful overlap; listed for completeness.
